feed.title: Merlin Schema
feed.subtitle: Authoritative documentation for the Merlin command-palette and voice-assistant schema used across the HAX ecosystem.

entry.title: Overview
entry.content:
Merlin is the universal command-palette and voice assistant in the HAX ecosystem. It is implemented by the <super-daemon> web component — a global singleton (globalThis.SuperDaemonManager) that surfaces a searchable palette of commands and a debounced, multi-step "program" engine. Users open it with Alt+Shift (or Meta+Shift on macOS). The persona name "Merlin" appears in voice prompts, UI copy, and throughout the codebase.

Merlin is used across HAXcms (site operations, admin panels, page editing), the HAX body (content authoring), and app-hax (the application shell). Any part of the application can register commands into the single shared palette, and those commands are filtered by the active "context" so the user only sees what is relevant.

This site documents the schema/contract for the two data structures that plug into Merlin — the Option and the Program — so that AI agents and human contributors can register and build Merlin commands without reverse-engineering the source.

Core concepts

Merlin has two kinds of registrable commands:

  • Option — a static, searchable command. It appears in the palette list; selecting it fires a single CustomEvent and (usually) closes the palette. Registered via SuperDaemonInstance.defineOption(option).
  • Program — a dynamic, search-driven command. Selecting its entry row launches "program mode": an async function is invoked with the user's search text, and the array of Option-shaped rows it returns replaces the top-level list. The function is re-invoked (debounced ~150ms) on every keystroke, so the results live-update as the user types. A Program is just an Option whose eventName is "super-daemon-run-program" and whose value.program is that async function.

The singleton access pattern

Merlin is a single shared instance. Get a reference to it like this:

Then register commands:

The registration call

defineOption(option) does light validation (requires value, title, eventName) and then auto-builds a searchable index string from the option's other fields. It pushes the option into allItems. Options can be registered at any time — most are registered in an element's firstUpdated() or on module load.

Where the runtime implementation lives

This spec is documentation only. The code that consumes this schema lives in the webcomponents monorepo, primarily elements/super-daemon/super-daemon.js (the singleton), the UI in lib/super-daemon-ui.js/lib/super-daemon-row.js/lib/super-daemon-search.js, and real Program factory modules under elements/haxcms-elements/lib/core/utils/*Program.js.

entry.title: Option Schema Reference
entry.content:
Required fields: title, value, eventName.

Required fields

  • title (string) — Primary display label. Used for alphabetical sort and exact-match priority boosting.
  • value (object) — Payload dispatched as the detail of the CustomEvent named by eventName. Shape varies by eventName.
  • eventName (string) — Name of the CustomEvent dispatched when the row is selected.

Display and search fields

  • icon (string, optional) — Icon name (e.g. "icons:save", "hax:wizard-hat") rendered by simple-icon-lite.
  • image (string, optional) — Image URL rendered in the row as an alternative to icon.
  • textCharacter (string, optional) — A single character or emoji rendered as an alternative to icon/image (e.g. "🍌").
  • tags (string[], optional, default []) — Searchable keyword tags. Also rendered as simple-tag chips in the row.
  • path (string, optional, default "") — Breadcrumb-style location string (e.g. "CMS/admin/seo"). Searchable as a whole phrase and split on /.
  • description (string, optional) — Extra searchable text. Indexed for search but not rendered.
  • priority (number, optional, default 0) — Sort weight. Lower numbers sort higher. Negative values boost prominence. An exact title match forces -10000000.
  • more (lit-html TemplateResult, optional) — Extra detail rendered in an expandable <details> section of the row. Only a plain string more is added to the search index.

Visibility and behavior fields

  • context (string | string[], optional, default "*") — Visibility scope. "*" means available in every context. Other common values: "CMS", "HAX", "admin", "logged-in", "community", ">" (developer mode), "/" (program list), and platform feature names ("addPage", "uploadMedia", "outlineDesigner") that disappear when HAXcms platform settings disable the feature. Prefer an array; a string is matched by substring.
  • inline (boolean, optional, default false) — Also list the option when Merlin is invoked inline (slash in an empty block, :: token, RTE toolbar button).
  • inlineOnly (boolean, optional, default false) — List the option only when Merlin is invoked inline; never in global browse/search. Implies inline, so don't set both.
  • externalLink (boolean, optional, default false) — Renders an open-in-new-window icon on the row (the option opens an external site).
  • hidden (boolean, optional) — When true, the option is registered and invokable by machineName/shortcut but excluded from browse/search results.

Voice and shortcut fields

  • voice (string, optional, falls back to title) — Voice-command phrase pattern for the hal-9000 speech layer, e.g. "(toggle) dark mode". Parenthesized segments are optional words.
  • shortcut (string | object, optional) — Keyboard-shortcut metadata linking the option to the shared KeyboardShortcutManager registry. Either a registry id string (e.g. "cms-save") or an inline descriptor object. Resolved to shortcutLabel; both excluded from the search index.

Auto-built fields (do not set yourself)

  • index (string, auto) — A space-joined, de-duplicated, lowercased search index derived from tags/path/title/voice/more/context plus the full path phrase.
  • shortcutLabel (string, auto) — Human-readable label from KeyboardShortcutManager.getLabel() (e.g. "Ctrl⇧S", "###"). Program result rows are not passed through defineOption(), so a row that wants a key hint sets it directly.

entry.title: Program Schema Reference
entry.content:
A Program is an Option with eventName: "super-daemon-run-program" and a value object containing the following keys.

value object fields

  • name (string, required) — Human-readable name shown as the program-mode title while the program is active.
  • program (async (input, values) => Promise<Option[]>, required) — The search function. input is the current search text; values is the bag passed into runProgram(). Each returned item is an Option-shaped row rendered by super-daemon-row. Re-invoked (debounced ~150ms) on every keystroke.
  • machineName (string, optional) — Stable identifier enabling runProgram('like', context, values, 'machineName') to resolve and invoke this program by name without holding a direct function reference.
  • context (string, optional) — Command context to activate when the program launches (e.g. "CMS" or ">"). A single string, not an array: runProgram() assigns it straight to commandContext.
  • placeholder (string, optional) — Placeholder text for the search input while the program is active (e.g. "Enter new title").
  • initialValue (async (values) => Promise<string>, optional) — Optional prefill: a non-empty string return pre-fills the search input when the program is launched with no explicit like/search. Currently only honored when the program is launched by machineName; selecting the row from Merlin search passes the function directly and skips it.

The whole value object is also the program's second argument (values), so any extra keys you put on value reach the program.

The lazy factory pattern

Programs are commonly lazy-loaded via dynamic import() of a createXProgram(context) factory module, so the program code is only fetched when the user actually selects it:

The factory module exports a createXProgram(context) function that returns the actual async (input, values) => [...] function, closing over context (typically the haxcms-site-editor-ui instance) so the program can call back into editor methods.

What a program returns

The program function returns an array of Option-shaped rows. Each row follows the same Option schema and is rendered by super-daemon-row. A common pattern is to return "confirm" rows that use eventName: "super-daemon-element-method" to dispatch a save event:

runProgram() — invoking a program programmatically

Programs can also be launched from code (not just by user search), via SuperDaemonInstance.runProgram():

When program is a string, runProgram looks up the matching value.machineName in allItems to resolve the function. The waveWand(params, target, sound) helper wraps runProgram + open() + an optional sound for the common "open Merlin in mini/wand mode near a target" interaction pattern.

entry.title: Event Contract & Context System
entry.content:
Event contract

When a result row is selected, super-daemon-row.selected() always dispatches a super-daemon-row-selected event (with detail = the row element), then dispatches a CustomEvent named option.eventName with detail set to option.value. For any eventName other than super-daemon-run-program, it also dispatches super-daemon-close to close the palette. Program selections keep the palette open so the user can continue interacting.

The super-daemon singleton listens for these events globally and routes them:

eventName routing table

  • super-daemon-element-method — Calls value.target[value.method](...value.args). Closes palette.
  • super-daemon-element-click — Dispatches a synthetic MouseEvent("click") on value.target. Closes palette.
  • super-daemon-run-program — Hands value to runProgram() — enters program mode. Does not close palette.
  • hax-super-daemon-insert-tag — HAXStore inserts a block: fills a waiting program target with properties.src/source/href, otherwise inserts through the tray (value: { value: tag, eventName: "insert-tag", demoSchema: true } or { properties, content }). Closes palette.
  • execute-keyboard-shortcut — haxcms-site-editor-ui resolves value.shortcutId in KeyboardShortcutManager and runs it. Closes palette.
  • disabled — No-op. Used for informational rows like "No active page found". Closes palette.
  • super-daemon-noop — No-op instruction row (no listener). Closes palette.
  • anything else — Dispatched as a plain CustomEvent; you need your own listener. Closes palette.

Other events the singleton listens for (dispatch these to drive Merlin from code):

Other listened events

  • super-daemon-define-option — detail is treated as an Option and registered via defineOption().
  • super-daemon-run-program — detail ({ program, context, name, placeholder, values }) launches a program.
  • super-daemon-element-method — detail ({ target, method, args }) invokes a method on a target.
  • super-daemon-element-click — detail ({ target }) clicks a target.
  • super-daemon-close — Closes the palette and resets state.
  • super-daemon-program-enter — detail ({ programName, input }) handles Enter pressed with no filtered results (used by the create-page program).
  • super-daemon-voice-command — detail ({ command, callback, context }) registers a voice command.

Context system

Every Option declares a context — a string or array of strings that determines when it is visible. The singleton tracks an active commandContext (a single string) and a context array (the set of contexts the current page/app state provides). An option appears only when its context intersects the active set.

Context values

  • * — Global — always available (the default when context is omitted).
  • CMS — Available while in the HAXcms site-editor context.
  • HAX — Available while in the HAX body editor (authoring) context.
  • admin — Available for admin/site-settings operations.
  • logged-in — Available only when the user is authenticated.
  • > — Developer mode — a special context entered by typing > in the palette.

The user switches the active commandContext by typing a prefix character (/, *, or >) into the search input, or via voice ("run program" → /, "developer mode" → >). When commandContext is "*" (global browse), options are filtered against the page's context array; when it is a specific value, only options whose context includes that value are shown.

entry.title: Voice & Shortcut Metadata
entry.content:
Voice command layer (optional facet)

When voiceSearch is enabled on the super-daemon element, the hal-9000 speech engine is loaded and Merlin's commands become voice-addressable. Each Option can declare a voice phrase pattern; if omitted, the title is used. The pattern syntax uses parenthesized segments for optional words, e.g. "(toggle) dark mode" matches both "toggle dark mode" and "dark mode".

Voice commands are re-processed (reprocessVoiceCommands()) whenever the visible item set changes (e.g. context switch), so only currently-relevant options are voice-addressable. A built-in catch-all ("*anything") routes unrecognized speech into the search input.

This layer is optional — Options and Programs work fully without it. The voice field is purely additive.

Shortcut metadata (optional facet)

An Option (or Program entry row) can declare a shortcut field that links it to the shared KeyboardShortcutManager registry — the single source of truth for keyboard/insertion shortcuts across the HAX ecosystem. That registry is also used by HAXcms Ctrl+Shift+[Key] bindings and the HAXStore markdown-trigger-to-gizmo map, so a Merlin option can reference the same shortcut descriptor those subsystems use.

shortcut accepts either a registry id string (e.g. "cms-save") — resolves to a descriptor previously registered via KeyboardShortcutManagerInstance.register(...) — or an inline descriptor object with the canonical shape:

When shortcut is present, defineOption() resolves a human-readable label via KeyboardShortcutManager.getLabel() and stores it on shortcutLabel (e.g. "Ctrl⇧S" for a binding, "###" for a markdown trigger). The UI reads shortcutLabel to render a keyboard hint in the row. Both shortcut and shortcutLabel are excluded from the search index so they don't pollute text matching.

This layer is optional — the shortcut field is purely additive and does not change how an option is invoked; it only surfaces a keyboard-hint label in the UI and (optionally) ties the option to a shared descriptor for cross-subsystem consistency.

entry.title: Rules & Minimal Samples
entry.content:
Rules for tools and agents registering Merlin commands

  1. Required: title, value, eventName. defineOption() silently ignores options missing any of them.
  2. Match value to eventName: {target, method, args?} for super-daemon-element-method, {target} for super-daemon-element-click, {name, program, ...} for super-daemon-run-program, {shortcutId} for execute-keyboard-shortcut.
  3. Use arrays for context (["CMS"]). A string context is matched with String.includes, so it matches by substring. Program value.context is the opposite: one string, because it becomes the active command context.
  4. Never set index, and don't set shortcutLabel on registered options: defineOption() builds both. Program result rows skip defineOption(), so set shortcutLabel there yourself if you want a key hint.
  5. Pick inline or inlineOnly, not both. hidden and inlineOnly programs need a machineName, because that's the only way to launch them.
  6. No unknown keys. Custom keys must start with x-, and remember every string field (including x- ones) goes into the search index.
  7. Scan before you finish: merlin-validate --scan <file>.

Minimal working sample

Validation

Merlin options are JS objects in source files, so the most useful check is the static scan:

--scan validates every *.defineOption({...}) object literal as a registered option and every other object literal with title + eventName + value as a Program result row. Values that are not literals (this.t.save, function references, lit templates) are accepted as-is; literal values, keys and value shapes are checked. JSON files are validated without --scan; add --rows for arrays of Program result rows and --json for a structured report.

entry.title: More Schemas
entry.content:
merlin-schema is one of several schema specifications in the HAX ecosystem. Explore the others:

  • JSON Outline Schema — the content structure, site navigation, and metadata schema used by HAXcms.
  • HAX Schema — the full haxProperties contract for element authoring.
  • HAX Element Schema — the lightweight virtual DOM object format used for demoSchema, insertion, and conversion workflows.
  • Appstore Spec — the schema for external media providers, upload targets, stax templates, and autoloaded elements.
